title: Getting started with FGstab
text: FGstab implements Integrated Path Stability Selection (IPSS) high-dimensional variable selection Fine-Gray competing risks regression model. method extends stability selection framework Meinshausen & Bühlmann (2010) penalised Fine-Gray estimator. core idea simple: instead fitting single LASSO model, data repeatedly split half LASSO Fine-Gray model fitted half-sample across grid regularisation values λ\lambda. selection frequency feature — proportion half-samples receives non-zero coefficient — tracked along path. Features consistently selected across many subsamples many values λ\lambda considered reliable.

title: Getting started with FGstab
code: remotes::install_github("hugocannafarina/FGstab") library(FGstab)

title: Getting started with FGstab
text: sim_competing() generates synthetic data Fine-Gray model user-controlled covariance structure. use independent design simplicity. outcome matrix y passed FGstab() must two columns: observed time event type (0 = censored, 1 = event interest, 2 = competing event).
code: set.seed(42) dat <- sim_competing(   n_ind       = 200,   n_pred      = 10,   n_var       = 300,   design      = "independent",   censor_rate = 0.3 )  # dat$X               — covariate matrix (200 x 300), centred and scaled # dat$surv            — data frame: Tobs, evtype (0/1/2), id # dat$true_pred_index — indices of the 10 truly predictive features # dat$beta            — true coefficient vector  table(dat$surv$evtype) #>  #>  0  1  2  #> 60 81 59 y <- cbind(time = dat$surv$Tobs, status = dat$surv$evtype)

title: Getting started with FGstab
text: B=100B = 100 subsampling iterations, data split two halves size ⌊n/2⌋\lfloor n/2 \rfloor. half, LASSO Fine-Gray model fitted grid λ\lambda values λmax\lambda_{\max} (feature selected) 0.05⋅λmax0.05 \cdot \lambda_{\max}. selection frequency feature jj regularisation parameter λ\lambda : Π̂j(λ)=12B∑k=12B𝟏[β̂j(k)(λ)≠0] \hat{\Pi}_j(\lambda) = \frac{1}{2B} \sum_{k=1}^{2B}   \mathbf{1}\!\left[\hat{\beta}_j^{(k)}(\lambda) \neq 0\right] Plotting Π̂j(λ)\hat{\Pi}_j(\lambda) 1/λ1/\lambda yields stability path feature jj. Features high maximum selection probability across path reliably associated outcome.

what: IPSS scores and the EFP bound
title: Getting started with FGstab
text: IPSS integrates stability paths produce score feature upper-bounds expected number false positives (EFP). bound depends choice bounding function hmh_m (controlled ipss_function): hm(π)={0if π≤0.5(2π−1)mif π>0.5 h_m(\pi) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{} \pi \leq 0.5 \\ (2\pi - 1)^m & \text{} \pi > 0.5 \end{cases} m=1m = 1 ("h1"), m=2m = 2 ("h2", default), m=3m = 3 ("h3"). Higher mm gives tighter conservative bound. integrated bound : EFP̂≤Ψ̂Sj \widehat{\mathrm{EFP}} \leq \frac{\hat{\Psi}}{S_j} Ψ̂\hat{\Psi} integrated upper bound expected number false positives (function BB, pp, mm), SjS_j integrated stability path feature jj transformed hmh_m. EFP score feature jj defined : EFPj=Ψ̂max⁡(Sj,Ψ̂/p) \mathrm{EFP}_j = \frac{\hat{\Psi}}{\max(S_j,\, \hat{\Psi}/p)} low EFP score means selecting feature jj implies small expected number false positives selected set.

title: Getting started with FGstab
text: Q-values derived EFP scores analogously Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. q-value feature jj minimum FDR achievable selected sets include feature jj: qj=mint:EFPt≤EFPjmaxk:EFPk≤tEFPk|{k:EFPk≤t}| q_j = \min_{t \,:\, \mathrm{EFP}_t \leq \mathrm{EFP}_j}   \frac{\max_{k:\, \mathrm{EFP}_k \leq t} \mathrm{EFP}_k}{|\{k : \mathrm{EFP}_k \leq t\}|}

title: Getting started with FGstab
text: result contains efp_scores q_values features, can inspect choosing threshold:
code: res <- FGstab(   X             = dat$X,   y             = y,   n_alphas      = 15,   ipss_function = "h2",   n_jobs        = 1        # set higher in practice ) print(res) #> === FGstab Result (IPSS) === #> Features tested  : 300  #> Features selected: 9  #> Selected indices : 13, 16, 36, 40, 192, 212, 234, 255, 288 # 10 most stable features (lowest EFP scores) efp_sorted <- sort(unlist(res$efp_scores)) head(round(efp_sorted, 4), 10) #>    288     36    255     16     13     40    234    192    212    175  #> 0.0556 0.0622 0.0669 0.1250 0.1394 0.2420 0.2981 0.3299 0.5814 8.8899

what: Controlling the expected number of false positives
title: Getting started with FGstab
text: Setting target_fp = 1 selects features whose EFP score 1, meaning 1 false positive expected selected set average.
code: res_fp <- FGstab(dat$X, y, n_alphas = 15, target_fp = 1, n_jobs = 1) print(res_fp) #> === FGstab Result (IPSS) === #> Features tested  : 300  #> Features selected: 9  #> Selected indices : 13, 16, 36, 40, 192, 212, 234, 255, 288  # How many true positives did we recover? tp <- sum(res_fp$selected_features %in% dat$true_pred_index) fp <- length(res_fp$selected_features) - tp cat("True positives :", tp, "\n") #> True positives : 8 cat("False positives:", fp, "\n") #> False positives: 1

title: Getting started with FGstab
text: Setting target_fdr = 0.2 selects features whose q-value 0.2.

title: Getting started with FGstab
text: competing events, FGstab() equivalent IPSS penalised Cox model. Use sim_survival() simulate data setting — output format identical sim_competing() evtype takes values 0 (censored) 1 (event).
code: dat_cox <- sim_survival(n_ind = 200, n_pred = 10, n_var = 300,                         design = "independent") y_cox   <- as.matrix(dat_cox$surv[, c("Tobs", "evtype")])  res_cox <- FGstab(dat_cox$X, y_cox, n_alphas = 15, target_fdr = 0.2, n_jobs = 1) print(res_cox) #> === FGstab Result (IPSS) === #> Features tested  : 300  #> Features selected: 6  #> Selected indices : 21, 51, 93, 117, 125, 254

what: FGstab — Stability Selection for the Fine-Gray Model
title: FGstab — Stability Selection for the Fine-Gray Model
text: Stability-based variable selection Fine-Gray competing risks model FGstab provides reliable sparse variable selection high-dimensional competing risks survival data. implements Integrated Path Stability Selection (IPSS) (Melikechi & Miller, 2026) penalised Fine-Gray model, extending stability selection framework Meinshausen & Bühlmann (2010) competing risks regression. method aggregates selection frequencies along LASSO regularisation path bounds expected number false positives false discovery rate via path integration. also supports standard survival data competing event, case reduces IPSS penalised Cox model.

code: library(FGstab) set.seed(1)  # Simulate data: 150 individuals, 8 true predictors, 300 total variables dat <- sim_competing(n_ind = 150, n_pred = 8, n_var = 300,                      design = "independent") y <- cbind(time = dat$surv$Tobs, status = dat$surv$evtype)  # Run IPSS — returns scores without automatic selection res <- FGstab(dat$X, y, n_alphas = 15) print(res) plot(res)  # Select features controlling the expected number of false positives res_fp <- FGstab(dat$X, y, n_alphas = 15, target_fp = 1) print(res_fp)  # Select features controlling the FDR res_fdr <- FGstab(dat$X, y, n_alphas = 15, target_fdr = 0.2) summary(res_fdr)

what: Variable Selection via IPSS for the Penalised Fine-Gray Model — FGstab
title: Variable Selection via IPSS for the Penalised Fine-Gray Model — FGstab
text: Implements Integrated Path Stability Selection (IPSS) (Melikechi & Miller, 2026) Fine-Gray competing-risks regression model. method repeatedly subsamples data, fits LASSO-penalised Fine-Gray model subsample across regularisation path, aggregates selection frequencies stability paths. EFP scores q-values derived integrated paths control either expected number false positives (target_fp) false discovery rate (target_fdr). y[, 2] contains 0 1 (competing event), Fine-Gray model reduces Cox model; FGstab performs IPSS penalised Cox regression. See sim_survival simulate data setting.

title: Variable Selection via IPSS for the Penalised Fine-Gray Model — FGstab
text: X Numeric matrix covariates, dimensions n x p. Used -(internal standardisation). y Two-column numeric matrix. first column must contain event time (observed follow-time). second column must contain event type indicator: 0 = censored, 1 = event interest, 2 = competing event (omit 2 standard survival / Cox setting). n_alphas Integer. Number regularisation values (lambda) path. Default 15. B Integer. Number subsampling iterations. Default 50. target_fp Numeric NULL. Maximum expected number false positives. Features EFP score \(\leq\) target_fp selected. Ignored target_fdr also provided. Default NULL. target_fdr Numeric \((0, 1)\) NULL. Maximum false discovery rate. Features q-value \(\leq\) target_fdr selected. Takes priority target_fp. Default 0.1. ipss_function Character string. IPSS bounding function controlling conservatism. One "h1", "h2" (default), "h3". "h3" least conservative. n_jobs Integer. Number cores parallel subsampling. Defaults detectCores() - 1.

what: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
text: Generates synthetic dataset competing risks model two event types (event interest competing event), following sub-distribution hazard model Fine Gray (1999). Covariates \(X \\mathbb{R}^{n \times p}\) drawn multivariate normal distribution \(X \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)\) whose covariance structure \(\Sigma\) controlled design argument.

title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
code: sim_competing(   n_ind = 250L,   n_pred = 10L,   n_var = 5000L,   censor_rate = 0.3,   design = c("independent", "toeplitz", "block"),   rho = 0.9 )

title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
text: n_ind Integer. Number individuals. Default 250. n_pred Integer. Number truly predictive covariates (\(|\mathcal{S}|\)). Default 10. n_var Integer. Total number covariates (\(p\)). Default 5000. censor_rate Numeric \([0, 1)\). Target proportion censored observations. Default 0.3. design Character string. Covariance structure \(\Sigma\). One "independent", "toeplitz", "block". See Covariance structures section details. rho Numeric \((0, 1)\). Decay parameter "toeplitz" design. Ignored designs. Default 0.9.

title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
text: named list four elements: X Numeric matrix covariates (n_ind x       n_var), centred scaled. surv Data frame columns Tobs (observed time),       evtype (0 = censored, 1 = event interest, 2 = competing       event), id. true_pred_index Integer vector length n_pred:       indices truly predictive covariates (\(\mathcal{S}\)). beta Numeric vector true coefficients (length       n_var; non-zero true_pred_index).

title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
text: Independent ("independent") \(\Sigma = I_p\).     covariate drawn ..d. \(\mathcal{N}(0, 1)\). Toeplitz ("toeplitz") $$\Sigma_{jk} = \rho^{|j - k|}, \quad j, k = 1, \ldots, p.$$     Correlations decay exponentially distance indices.     parameter rho \(\(0, 1)\) controls decay rate:     values close 1 yield strongly correlated neighbouring covariates,     values close 0 approach independent design. Block ("block") $$       \Sigma_{jk} = \begin{cases}         1   & \text{} j = k, \\         0.5 & \text{} j \neq k \text{ }                        \lfloor j / B \rfloor = \lfloor k / B \rfloor, \\         0   & \text{otherwise,}       \end{cases}     $$     \(B = 10\) block size. Covariates within block     share fixed pairwise correlation 0.5; covariates different     blocks independent.

title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing
text: True coefficients \(\beta \\mathbb{R}^p\) sparse: n_pred indices drawn uniformly random assigned coefficients \(\mathcal{U}(-1, 1)\); coefficients zero. marginal probability event interest individual \(\) $$   \pi_i = 1 - (1 - \pi_0)^{\exp(X_i^\top \beta)}, $$ \(\pi_0 = 0.75\) baseline event rate. Event times event interest drawn via quantile inversion sub-distribution function; competing event times drawn \(\mathrm{Exp}(\text{rate} = 3)\). Censoring applied thresholding censor_rate quantile observed times.

title: Simulate competing risks data under the Fine-Gray model — sim_competing

title: Simulate survival data under the Cox proportional hazards model — sim_survival
text: Generates synthetic dataset standard survival model competing risks, following Cox proportional hazards model exponential baseline hazard. Covariates \(X \\mathbb{R}^{n \times p}\) drawn multivariate normal distribution \(X \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)\) whose covariance structure \(\Sigma\) controlled design argument (options sim_competing).

title: Simulate survival data under the Cox proportional hazards model — sim_survival
code: sim_survival(   n_ind = 250L,   n_pred = 10L,   n_var = 5000L,   censor_rate = 0.3,   design = c("independent", "toeplitz", "block"),   rho = 0.9 )

title: Simulate survival data under the Cox proportional hazards model — sim_survival
text: n_ind Integer. Number individuals. Default 250. n_pred Integer. Number truly predictive covariates (\(|\mathcal{S}|\)). Default 10. n_var Integer. Total number covariates (\(p\)). Default 5000. censor_rate Numeric \([0, 1)\). Target proportion censored observations. Default 0.3. design Character string. Covariance structure \(\Sigma\). One "independent", "toeplitz", "block". See Covariance structures section details. rho Numeric \((0, 1)\). Decay parameter "toeplitz" design. Ignored designs. Default 0.9.

title: Simulate survival data under the Cox proportional hazards model — sim_survival
text: named list four elements: X Numeric matrix covariates (n_ind x       n_var), centred scaled. surv Data frame columns Tobs (observed time),       evtype (0 = censored, 1 = event), id. true_pred_index Integer vector length n_pred:       indices truly predictive covariates (\(\mathcal{S}\)). beta Numeric vector true coefficients (length       n_var; non-zero true_pred_index).

title: Simulate survival data under the Cox proportional hazards model — sim_survival
text: True coefficients \(\beta \\mathbb{R}^p\) sparse: n_pred indices drawn uniformly random assigned coefficients \(\mathcal{U}(-1, 1)\); coefficients zero. Event times drawn exponential distribution rate \(\exp(X_i^\top \beta)\): $$T_i \sim \mathrm{Exp}\!\left(\exp(X_i^\top \beta)\right).$$ corresponds Cox model unit exponential baseline hazard. Censoring applied thresholding censor_rate quantile observed times. output formatted identically sim_competing evtype \(\\{0, 1\}\) (competing event), can passed directly FGstab, operates IPSS Cox model.
